clue.text: But do we hear reports of its taking off?

definitions.text: But do we hear reports of its taking off?

parts.words: But do we hear reports of its taking off?
parts.note: the reports sound like gunshots from a firearm, and taking off suggests a bird flying up, so the name joins a gun to a bird

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether take-offs, of planes perhaps, come with loud bangs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reports' reads as news or accounts but means bangs, as of a gun firing; the RIFLEBIRD is an Australasian bird of paradise.
explanation.definitionFit: The riflebird is a bird of paradise whose name pairs a gun, which makes reports, with a creature that takes off in flight.

clue.text: Groundwork in respect of south-east vault…

parts.note: re is the Latin-derived word meaning concerning or about
SE is the compass abbreviation for south-east
an arch is the curved structure of a vault

explanation.surface: A note on preparatory work about a vaulted building in the south-east of the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Background study done before a project is its preparation, the groundwork it rests on.

clue.text: … architect left inside, to struggle

indicators.note: the word inside tells us the letter for left goes within the word for architect

parts.note: a founder is the one who creates or devises something, its architect

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue, the architect is left floundering on the job.
explanation.definitionFit: To flounder is to flail about clumsily, which is a way to struggle.

clue.text: Playful gamine can be a problem

indicators.note: playful suggests the letters of gamine frolic about into a new order

explanation.surface: A frisky young woman may cause difficulties.
explanation.definitionFit: An enigma is a puzzle or mystery, a problem to be solved.

clue.text: Popular achievement, certainly!

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a deed is a feat or achievement

explanation.surface: An exclamation agreeing that a well-liked accomplishment was impressive.
explanation.definitionFit: Indeed is an emphatic word of agreement, like truly or certainly.

clue.text: Stream of abuse from girl before a race

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, short for Diana
a tribe is a race or people

explanation.surface: A girl shouting insults before a running race starts.
explanation.definitionFit: A diatribe is a bitter verbal attack, a torrent of invective.

clue.text: Out of the country for the most part

indicators.note: most part means only the greater portion of the words for the is kept, so the answer lies within them, the final letter going

explanation.surface: Someone is abroad most of the time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For the most part' reads as 'mostly', but it is FOR THE with its last letter dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Forth can mean away, out or abroad, as in going forth from one's homeland.

clue.text: Weakest charge favoured, would you say?

indicators.note: would you say asks us to hear the two words spoken rather than read them

parts.note: a charge is a fee, and favoured is blessed, which can be said as one syllable, blest

explanation.surface: A question about whether the cheapest fee was the one chosen, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Would you say?' signals sound: fee plus blessed, said with a one-syllable ending, gives the superlative of feeble.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeblest is the superlative of feeble, meaning the least strong.

clue.text: Border, batting, gets a single here in Italy

parts.note: a rim is an edge or border
in cricket the side batting is said to be in
I is the Roman numeral one, a single

explanation.surface: A cricket picture: a batsman near the boundary takes a single run.
explanation.walkthrough: RIMINI is a seaside resort on Italy's Adriatic coast; 'batting' for IN is a cricket usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Rimini is a town on the Italian coast, so it fits a place indicated as being in Italy.

clue.text: Dash from Baden-Baden, for example

parts.note: the dash is not a hurried departure from the German spa town but the little line joining its two halves in print

explanation.surface: A traveller hurries away from the German spa town.
explanation.definitionFit: A short horizontal joining mark, as in the doubled spa name, is a punctuation dash of the linking kind.

clue.text: Having floors, we hear, decorated with narrative scenes

definitions.meaning: a building with floors is storeyed, which is pronounced the same way
a ... frieze or window is ornamented with pictures telling tales

explanation.surface: A building with several levels whose walls are painted with tales.
explanation.definitionFit: Storied means celebrated in tales or adorned with depictions of them, and sounds like storeyed, multi-level.

clue.text: Habit less breakable, it is found

indicators.note: breakable suggests the letters of habit less can be broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A habit is easier to break once you know about it, apparently.
explanation.definitionFit: To found a company is to set it up, create it.

clue.text: Man is sent off with it, for a day at the racecourse

definitions.text: Man is sent off with it, for a day at the racecourse

parts.words: Man is sent off with it, for a day at the racecourse
parts.note: sent off reads as being waved away on a jaunt to the races, but it is the football punishment that sends a player from the pitch

explanation.surface: A man is packed off to the races for the day with his programme in hand.
explanation.walkthrough: A racecard is the programme at a race meeting, which the surface wants; the football sense is the real one.
explanation.definitionFit: A referee shows this coloured penalty card to dismiss a player from the field.

clue.text: French composer kept short by Scotsman and Portuguese, possibly

indicators.note: kept short means the composer's name loses its final letter

parts.note: Jacques Ibert was a French composer
Ian is a typical Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: A French composer is curtailed by a Scot and possibly a Portuguese person.
explanation.definitionFit: A Portuguese person lives on the peninsula shared with Spain, so is an example of someone from that peninsula.

clue.text: Vast, lavish fete about end of September

definitions.text: Vast, lavish fete about end of September

indicators.note: about signals that the letters of the three words plus one more are moved round
end of picks the final letter of September

explanation.surface: A huge, extravagant party held around the close of September.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' rearranges VAST LAVISH FETE together with R, the last letter of September; the whole clue also describes the event.
explanation.definitionFit: The church thanksgiving for the gathered crops is held near the close of September with a festive spread.

clue.text: Lucky England openers capable of becoming useful

parts.note: the opening letters of England are E and N
viable means workable, able to succeed in practice

explanation.surface: England's opening batsmen are fortunate and could turn out to be handy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Openers' suggests cricket's opening batsmen but takes the first two letters of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Enviable describes something others would covet, as a fortunate position is.

clue.text: Flavour not entirely rich, but delicate

parts.note: taste means flavour

indicators.note: not entirely means the word for rich loses its last letter

parts.note: full, as in full-bodied, means rich

explanation.surface: A food critic's verdict: the flavour isn't overpowering but subtle.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasteful means refined and restrained, showing delicate judgment.

clue.text: Sort of blind like Titian, for example

definitions.meaning: a window blind with horizontal slats is named after a city of Italy
Titian was a painter from that Italian city

explanation.surface: Window coverings in the style of a Renaissance painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Venetian names both a slatted window blind and things from Venice, as the painter Titian was.

clue.text: Residue of Svengali's settlement

indicators.note: settlement suggests the letters of the name settle into a new order

parts.note: the possessive s adds no letter; Svengali is the mesmerist of the novel Trilby

explanation.surface: What remains of the hypnotist's property after an agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: Leavings are what is left over, the remnants or residue.

clue.text: Puts aside space for books

definitions.meaning: to shelve a plan is to postpone or set it aside

explanation.surface: Someone sets things aside to make room on the bookcase.
explanation.definitionFit: Shelves as a verb means postpones or defers; as a noun the ledges hold volumes.

clue.text: Small plastic bag long in street

indicators.note: in tells us the word for long is placed within the abbreviation for street

parts.note: to ache is to long or yearn

explanation.surface: Someone yearns for a little plastic packet out in the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A sachet is a small sealed packet, often of shampoo or sauce.

clue.text: Uprightness of actor's body, say?

definitions.meaning: the British performers' trade union is called ..., so a body for actors

explanation.surface: A question about the upright posture of an actor's physique.
explanation.definitionFit: Equity means fairness and justice, and is also the name of the UK actors' union.

clue.text: Domed house, in wild tundra, has nothing in it

indicators.note: in it puts the letter for nothing inside the rearranged letters
wild signals the letters of tundra run riot into a new order

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A domed dwelling out on the untamed tundra stands empty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' rearranges TUNDRA to RTUNDA, and 'in it' puts O inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotunda is a round building with a dome on top.

clue.text: Bath is one expedient

definitions.meaning: Bath is a spa town in Somerset, a holiday destination

explanation.surface: The city of Bath is a handy option.
explanation.walkthrough: BATH is a spa city in south-west England; the capital B is disguised at the start of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Resort means both a holiday town and a fallback measure one turns to.

clue.text: Family in name that is charming

indicators.note: in tells us the word for family goes within the word for name

parts.note: a tag is a label or name
kin means relatives, family

explanation.surface: A family name that is delightful.
explanation.definitionFit: A taking manner is one that captivates, attractive and appealing.

clue.text: Abroad, they made such a holy fuss!

definitions.text: Abroad, they made such a holy fuss!

parts.words: Abroad, they made such a holy fuss!
parts.note: a holy fuss is a campaign waged in the name of religion, carried out in foreign lands by medieval Christian knights

explanation.surface: Tourists overseas caused a great commotion over something sacred.
explanation.definitionFit: Medieval knights who marched to the Holy Land waged war for their faith in foreign parts.

clue.text: Round-wing angle

parts.note: O is round in shape
a pinion is a bird's wing

explanation.surface: A clipped phrase like a technical term for part of a building or wing.
explanation.definitionFit: An angle is a point of view or slant on something, an opinion.

clue.text: Shrub that grows in a filthy mess

indicators.note: in shows the answer sits within the words filthy mess

explanation.surface: A bush that thrives in muck.
explanation.definitionFit: Thyme is a small aromatic shrubby herb.

clue.text: Plaintiffs, perhaps, lasting it out?

indicators.note: out signals the letters of lasting it are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: People suing in court who hold out to the bitter end.
explanation.definitionFit: Plaintiffs are one kind of party to a lawsuit, so examples of those engaged in legal action.
